trend_source: This TikTok framing 'Sexy & Rich' as investing in yourself pulled 689.7k views and 192.9k likes, proving the self-investment angle resonates hard.
title: The best asset in your portfolio is you
hooks: The richest thing I ever invested in wasn't a stock, it was myself.
Everyone wants passive income before they've built a single skill.
Your earning power is the one asset nobody can crash for you.
talking_points: Skills raise your income, and income is the fuel for every other financial goal
Investing in yourself includes courses, health, and the habits that keep you working long
But protect the earner too: if your income stops, so does the plan, which is where income protection and savings matter
Balance growing yourself with putting some of that higher income to work each month
cta: Comment GROW and I'll share a simple worksheet to map your income, savings and protection in one page.
why_it_works: The self-investment message already went viral, and it honestly bridges to protecting your income, the foundation of any plan.
how_to_film: Talk straight to camera, medium close-up. Open with the hook flatly, no smile. Keep it punchy, one idea per breath, cut on each line.
author: @dananozime

trend_source: A US creator's 'five expensive things worth the money' finance edition hit 735.4k views and 164.6k likes. I adapt the accounts to Singapore.
title: Expensive things that are actually worth it in Singapore
hooks: Some expensive things are a waste, and some quietly pay you back for years.
I stopped feeling guilty about these five spends once I did the maths.
Cheap isn't always smart, here's where spending more actually pays off.
talking_points: Quality health cover you understand beats the cheapest option you'll never claim on properly
Good shoes, a solid mattress and health basics protect your ability to keep earning
Professional advice or upskilling that raises your income can outperform the fee many times over
An emergency fund isn't a 'thing' but it's the spend that buys you calm when life goes sideways
cta: Save this and share it with the friend who thinks every big spend is a scam.
why_it_works: The 'worth the money' list format is proven engaging, and it lets an advisor reframe protection and upskilling as smart spending, not guilt.
how_to_film: Count on your fingers, one item per beat. Fast cuts between each of the five. Open on the hook before any intro.
author: @brittlum

trend_source: A UK creator's 'financial freedom in 5 steps' with percentage benchmarks got 612.8k views and 22k likes. Figures are illustrative, so I tell viewers to adjust to their own life.
title: A simple percentage budget for your Singapore pay
hooks: Here's how to split your salary without tracking every single kopi.
Most people budget by feeling, then wonder where the money went.
One number decides how much you should spend on rent, food and transport.
talking_points: Cap essentials like housing, bills, food and transport at a set share of income so lifestyle doesn't creep
Ring-fence a guilt-free spending slice so the plan actually survives real life
Set targets for short-term savings and clearing any high-interest debt first
Automate a portion each month toward long-term goals and remember CPF and SRS are part of your picture

why_it_works: The percentage-benchmark format proved highly shareable, and it's honest educational content once localised to SGD and CPF.
how_to_film: Show the maths on-screen text as you speak each step. Steady pace, five clear beats. Start mid-sentence with the hook, no long intro.

trend_source: A Caleb Hammer clip of a man who spent nearly $1M building houses and still needs $500k more racked up 263k views and 8.6k likes. It's a US show but the lesson is universal.
title: The sunk cost trap that keeps draining your money
hooks: He sank a million dollars in and still needs half a million more.
The scariest words in money are 'I've come too far to stop now'.
Throwing good money after bad has a name, and it's costing you.
talking_points: Sunk cost fallacy: we keep funding a losing project because of what we already spent
Before adding money, ask what you'd decide if you were starting fresh today
Big commitments need a budget and an exit plan before you start, not after
A cash buffer stops one over-ambitious project from swallowing your whole financial life
cta: Comment STUCK if a money decision is dragging on and let's talk it through honestly.
why_it_works: The jaw-dropping number hooks viewers, and it teaches sunk cost without mocking anyone, just the mistake.
how_to_film: React-style: repeat the number with disbelief, then pivot to the lesson. Keep energy high early, slow down for the takeaway.
author: @dr.knowz

trend_source: A punchy 'if you want X you need Y' list from a US creator earned 56.7k views and 5.3k likes with a strong share rate. I drop the follow-me line.
title: What you actually need to get what you want
hooks: If you want freedom, you first need to make money, full stop.
Everyone wants the outcome, nobody wants the requirement.
Peace of mind isn't bought, it's built by clearing your debt.
talking_points: Income needs a skill, so invest in what makes you more valuable
Growth needs investing, and peace needs a debt-free base
Wealth needs patience because compounding rewards time, not timing
Retiring early needs one thing above all: starting now, even small
cta: Which one are you working on this year? Tell me in the comments.
why_it_works: The rhythmic want-versus-need structure is proven to hold attention and doubles as honest financial principles.

author: @justtonch

title: In case the internet made you forget what's normal
hooks: Taking a personal loan for your wedding is not normal.
You're not behind, you're keeping score in a game nobody else is playing.
Feeling like a failure for not owning a condo by 30? Let's talk.
talking_points: Financing luxuries you can't yet afford quietly became the baseline, but it isn't the norm
If it makes you happy and you can afford it, go ahead, the problem is doing it to keep up
Comparison spending sabotages the savings and protection that actually build security
Go at a pace you can afford; slower and yours beats fast and financed

why_it_works: The 'this is not normal' reality check went viral on the exact social pressure Singaporeans feel, and it validates instead of shaming.

trend_source: A Caleb Hammer clip of a man who owes his wife $200k yet financed a Lamborghini hit 216.4k views and 5.3k likes. It's a US show but the money lesson travels.
title: Never budgeting for tax is how the money disappears
hooks: Owing your wife 200k, then asking her to split a Lamborghini with you.
'I never have money for taxes' is not a personality, it's a plan problem.
The Lambo wasn't the mistake, forgetting the tax bill was.
talking_points: Self-employed and commission earners must set aside for tax before spending the rest
Lifestyle upgrades funded by debt while you owe others is borrowing from your future
Separate 'money I have' from 'money already spoken for' like tax and debt
A simple set-aside account for tax and irregular bills prevents the panic loan
cta: Comment TAX if you're self-employed and want a simple set-aside system that works.
why_it_works: The absurd Lambo-and-debt story hooks people, and it lets an advisor teach tax and debt discipline while punching up at the mistake, not a person.
how_to_film: Open with the disbelief hook, react briefly, then flip to the practical lesson. Keep it fast, land the tax point clearly at the end.

hooks: Some money advice is gospel online, but it doesn't fit everyone.

trend_source: A Singapore creator's honest take on why he bought a Continental car, and admitting he didn't need to, beat his usual views by about 10x at 13.4k views. Local context, local car costs.
title: Rewarding yourself without wrecking your plan
hooks: I'll be honest, I did not need a Conti car, and that's the whole point.
There's a right way to reward yourself after years of grinding.
A car in Singapore is a want dressed up as a need, let's be real about it.
talking_points: Rewards are healthy when they come after the plan is funded, not instead of it
Be honest about want versus need; a car can genuinely save time, but name the real reason
Set a 'reward budget' so the treat is planned, not a splurge that dents savings
Whatever your motivation, holidays, watches or a car, make sure future you is covered first
